props.title: Earthlings
props.initialSlug: Documentary about humanity's relationship with animals

sections.content: Earthlings (2005) stands as one of the most unflinching and influential animal rights documentaries ever made. Narrated by Joaquin Phoenix, it exposed industrial animal exploitation with raw footage that influenced later works like Dominion (2018) and Cowspiracy (2014). Its impact echoes through films like Food Inc. (2008) and Blackfish (2013), which similarly challenged viewers to confront uncomfortable realities about human treatment of animals. The film's graphic approach sparked intense debate about documentary ethics and shock value versus educational merit.

sections.content: The visual approach of Earthlings broke new ground in advocacy filmmaking. Rather than relying on expert interviews or statistics, director Shaun Monson let raw footage speak for itself, setting a template followed by What the Health (2017) and Land of Hope and Glory (2017). The film's structure - dividing content into five chapters reflecting different uses of animals - influenced how later documentaries organized complex ethical topics.

The film's impact extended beyond animal rights circles. An Inconvenient Truth (2006) and Before the Flood (2016) adopted similar strategies of using graphic imagery to spark environmental awareness. Earthlings also influenced celebrity activism in documentaries, paving the way for personalities like Leonardo DiCaprio and Ellen Page to narrate cause-driven films. movies.title: Blackfish
movies.slug: Documentary examining captive orcas that led to major changes at SeaWorld

sections.content: Modern investigative documentaries like The Game Changers (2018) and Seaspiracy (2021) follow Earthlings' (2005) blueprint of combining hidden camera footage with polished production values. The film's unflinching approach to difficult subject matter influenced a generation of documentarians to prioritize truth over comfort, seen in works like Unity (2015) - Monson's spiritual sequel.
